rachel_infra: Heads up — noticed a spike in preemptions in us-west1 yesterday morning. p4d spot pool preempt rate jumped to ~22% around 03:20 UTC, several Dedicated-backed queues hit coldstart cascades. Long-tail evictions (~4+ min) causing request backpressure. Need a quick procurement/mitigation plan before next rollout.
jordan_sre: Yikes. Any idea if this was price-driven or capacity-driven? Did you see auction price spikes or capacity constraint tags?
rachel_infra: Prices were stable. Provider health signals showed a 'capacity-constraint' flag for the p4d zones — looks like capacity-optimized pools got drained. My interim proposal: shift some allocation away from pure price-optimized pools, add a small warmbuffer (cross-region warm spares), and enable soft-evict/drain policies so we don't lose in-flight KV cache.
maya_sourcing: +1 to warmbuffer. Practical suggestion: keep ~5% non-preemptible or reserved warm nodes per shard, OR hold 8-10 hot p4d pre-warmed instances in us-west2 to absorb immediate failover. Rough cost tradeoff I estimate +6–9% on GPU spend but large drop in coldstart P99.
oliver_sched: We can also try a transient bid ramp: keep capacity-optimized as primary, but during autoscale windows briefly raise max-bid for 90–120s to lock capacity for the spike. Pseudocode: ```# bid-ramp logic
if scale_event_detected:
  for pool in capacity_preferred_pools:
    pool.bid = min(pool.max_bid * 1.2, global_price_cap)
  sleep(90)
  revert_bids()```
jordan_sre: Need to ensure graceful shutdown completes <30s else soft-evict won't help. Add preemption hook to checkpoint KV cache to redis, and a quick request-failover path to a smaller, quantized model variant (tf32->int8) for degraded quality but preserved latency.
rachel_infra: For immediate rollout: set warmbuffer to 7%, enable soft-evict TTL=45s, and add cross-region spillback to us-west2/us-central as secondary. Maya — can you run a quick cost + availability sim?
maya_sourcing: Running sim now. Preliminary: 7% warmbuffer + cross-region failover -> coldstarts down ~92% in the 1h spike test, 99th latency improves ~38ms. Incremental monthly cost ~+$1.6k for baseline fleet (depends on sustained usage). Detailed numbers in the spreadsheet I'm linking in the PR.
capacity-bot: autoscaler-sim: p4d_spot_loss -> spillback(us-west2) reduces 99p latency by 40ms and drops failed-starts by 87% in the synthetic load test.
oliver_sched: I'll submit a small PR to implement the transient-bid ramp and soft-evict hooks, plus a canary schedule for 02:00 UTC tomorrow. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/458 (placeholder). cc @jordan_sre
jordan_sre: :thumbsup: Also adding an alert: `spot_preempt_5min` -> fire if preempt rate >10% for 5m and failed_starts >5/min. This should catch the pattern faster.
rachel_infra: Thanks team. Action items: 1) Maya run full cost sim + update sheet; 2) Oliver push PR for bid ramp + soft-evict; 3) Jordan add alert + preemption-hook work; 4) I'll draft a short incident note and schedule follow-up postmortem. We'll re-evaluate after the canary.
